intended_object: The homogeneous (vanishing) ideal I([a]) of the projective point with homogeneous coordinates a in the polynomial ring k[X_i : i ∈ ι]. It is the ideal spanned by the homogeneous polynomials vanishing at a, equivalently the vanishing ideal of the line through a. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and its use as a point of Proj.
explanation: The body is the kernel of the k-algebra map k[X_i] → k[t] sending X i to a i · t. A polynomial F maps to Σ_d F_d(a)·t^d, where F_d is its homogeneous component of degree d. So F is in the kernel exactly when every homogeneous component of F vanishes at a, which is the standard definition of the homogeneous ideal of the point [a]. The file proves this characterisation for homogeneous F, that the ideal is homogeneous and prime, that it is relevant when a ≠ 0, and that it is unchanged when a is rescaled by a nonzero scalar. When a = 0 the kernel is the irrelevant ideal, which is a sensible value, and the library only uses the definition with a ≠ 0. The index type ι is fully general. The field hypothesis on k is the standard setting for points given by homogeneous coordinates, and the library needs it for primality (k[t] must be a domain) and for the descent to Projectivization. Mathlib has no ready-made homogeneous ideal of a projective point; MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal is the affine vanishing ideal, a different object.
